newsitem.title: USA: Iowa farmers plant half the corn crop in one week.
newsitem.headline: Iowa farmers plant half the corn crop in one week.

text.p: Iowa farmers planted nearly half the intended corn crop in the week ended Sunday, putting seedings about six days ahead of the five-year average, according to Iowa's Agriculture Statistics Service.

"Dry weather early in the week helped farmers get over half of the the corn crop planted and make significant progress on other field work," the report said. "Heavy rains on Wednesday and Friday kept farmers from making even more progress."
Corn plantings were 53 percent complete, up from four percent last week and 33 percent for the five-year average.
Oat plantings were nearing completion with 94 percent of the crop seeded, compared with 79 percent average.
Winter wheat conditions declined from the previous week with one percent rated very poor, four percent poor, 32 percent fair, 59 percent good and four percent excellent.
"Effects of the rough winter are being found in alfalfa, where areas of significant winterkill are now being reported in Iowa's northern three districts," the report said.
Pasture was rated one percent very poor, 10 poor, 36 fair, 45 good and eight percent excellent. Topsoil moisture was rated one percent short, 57 adequate and 42 surplus.
